name: Golden Gate Park
start_event: Park Act signed 4 Apr 1870 by state legislature; site surveyed by W.H. Hall 1870
planting_note: Dune reclamation began 1871 at east end (270 ac incl. Panhandle); 22,000 trees set out 1872, ~60,000 by 1875, 155,000 by 1879; ~600 ac west of Strawberry Hill forested later (Monterey pine/cypress, blue gum); largely mature by 1890; west end finished c.1900 (Beach Chalet 1900, windmills 1902-08)

name: Lake Merced Park
start_event: Officially designated a park run by Rec & Park in 1950 (city bought lake from Spring Valley Water Co. 1930)
planting_note: Harding Park golf course developed on leased Spring Valley land in 1920s; tracts near the lake forested 1900-1940 (1954 Planning report)

name: John McLaren Park
start_event: Supervisors voted 1926 to buy 550 ac; dedicated with tree-planting ceremony Dec 1927; land assembled 1928-46 (SNRAMP says dedicated 1934)
planting_note: Dedication tree planting 1927; WPA scenic drive and landscaping 1930s; most facilities built 1950-80; 2,290 seedlings planted 1965-66

name: San Francisco Zoo
start_event: Fleishhacker Zoo founded 1929 beside Fleishhacker Pool (1925) and playfield

name: Lincoln Park
start_event: Former city Golden Gate Cemetery (1868) turned over to Park Commission 1909; graves relocated
planting_note: Golf 3 holes 1902, 14 by 1914, 18 by 1917; Legion of Honor 1924; tract forested 1900-1940 (1954 Planning report)

name: Yacht Harbor and Marina Green
start_event: Yacht Harbor and North Gardens (now Marina Green) built for 1915 PPIE and acquired by city from the Exposition
planting_note: Green is lawn on PPIE fill; Montgomery/Marina airfield use from 1920; Gas House Cove bought 1939-49, harbor expanded mid-1960s

name: Glen Canyon Park
start_event: City purchased 101-ac canyon from Crocker Real Estate Co. 1922
planting_note: Blue gum windbreak from Sutro's 'Gum Tree Ranch' era; recreation center at south end (WPA era)

name: Crocker Amazon Playground
start_event: Recreation Commission given permission 1934 to develop the 55-ac Crocker Amazon reservoir site (PUC/Water Dept land)
planting_note: WPA built ballfields, bleachers and playground in 1930s; still being built out c.1940

name: Twin Peaks
start_event: City purchased the summits 1915 (park later grew to ~64 ac)
planting_note: Summits kept as grass/scrub; Sutro eucalyptus on lower slopes planted mid-1880s; Christmas Tree Point overlook 1985

name: Mt. Davidson Park
start_event: First 20 ac bought (purchase approved 1927); park dedicated 1929; +6 ac c.1934, +7 ac 1941, more 1950
planting_note: Forest planted on Adolph Sutro's land by schoolchildren/unemployed on first Arbor Days (from 1886); east slope left treeless

name: Bay View Park
start_event: Dedicated as a park 1915 (Burnham 1905 plan's 'Visitacion Park')
planting_note: Hill forested 1900-1940; WPA roadways and landscaping 1930s (1954 Planning report)

name: Buena Vista Park
start_event: Set aside 1867 as 'Hill Park' by Outside Lands committee; later renamed Buena Vista
planting_note: WPA paths with gutters of reused headstones 1930s

name: Sigmund Stern Recreation Grove
start_event: Donated to city by Rosalie Stern 1931; dedicated 4 Jun 1932
planting_note: Eucalyptus grove planted by the Greene family in 19th c.; WPA landscaping 1930s

name: Pine Lake Park
start_event: City bought lake and land within five years after Stern Grove opened in 1932 (exact year not found; range 1932-37)
planting_note: Eucalyptus around lake planted by Greene family (19th c.)

name: Bernal Heights Park
start_event: Rec & Park Commission voted 1972 to take hilltop from Public Works; transfer celebrated 10 Jun 1973; Prop J protection 1974
planting_note: Kept as open grassland; Bernal Heights Blvd ring road built 1935 (WPA)

name: Balboa Park
start_event: Dedicated 1909 on 100-ac House of Refuge lot (dedication ceremony 1910); western part given to City College 1936
planting_note: Development slowed by Ingleside Jail until 1934; forested 1900-1940 (1954 Planning report)

name: Interior Greenbelt
start_event: Purchased by the city in the 1950s (exact year not found; decade midpoint)
planting_note: Part of Sutro Forest: eucalyptus planted by Adolph Sutro from the 1880s; trail dates to 1880s

name: Lower Great Highway
start_event: Great Highway paved 1929 (1927 Boulevard Bond) with Lower GH service road east of old 1890s rail berm; Ocean Beach strip designated for public use in 1868 Outside Lands order
planting_note: O'Shaughnessy's Ocean Beach Esplanade completed 1928; median strip landscaped

name: Palace of Fine Arts
start_event: Built for 1915 Panama-Pacific Exposition (opened Feb 1915); only structure kept on site
planting_note: Lagoon landscape from 1915; rotunda rebuilt in concrete 1964-74; lagoon renovated 2009

name: West Sunset Playground
start_event: Playground and co-located schools opened 1954 (land first proposed 1930, planning 1946)

name: Park Presidio Blvd
start_event: Land purchased 1903 ($360,000) as extension of Golden Gate Park
planting_note: Grading and planting begun by 1910; widened and re-landscaped late 1930s as Golden Gate Bridge approach

name: Mission Dolores Park
start_event: City bought former Jewish cemeteries 1905 as 'Mission Park' (1903 ballot measure)
planting_note: Refugee camp 1906-08; planted terraces, tennis courts, athletic field by 1910

name: Louis Sutter Playground
start_event: Completed 1965 under McLaren Park 1959 master plan

name: St. Mary's Playground
start_event: WPA began shaping St. Mary's Recreation Area 1933 on former St. Mary's College land (subdivided 1924)
planting_note: WPA grading, rubble walls and landscaping 1933-34

name: Corona Heights
start_event: City purchased 16-ac Rock Hill 1941 ($27,333) and named it Corona Heights

name: Mountain Lake Park
start_event: 20 ac at Mountain Lake designated for a public park by Outside Lands committee (Order No. 800, 1868); Wikipedia gives c.1875 for Hall's design
planting_note: ~20,000 trees planted c.1890; WPA work 1930s; lake reduced by 1930s Park Presidio/MacArthur Tunnel fill

name: Alamo Square
start_event: Reserved in 1855 Van Ness Ordinance (Mayor Van Ness named it 1856; legislature confirmed 1858)
planting_note: Squatter evicted 1868; graded and landscaped with paths and walls 1892

name: Julius Kahn Playground
start_event: Playground named for Rep. Julius Kahn in 1926; on Presidio land under revocable federal permit (renamed Presidio Wall Playground 2019)

name: Midtown Terrace Playground
start_event: 2026-11: dedication ceremonies held Sat 20 Oct 1961 (commission minutes 26 Oct 1961). Earlier note: Built on covered Sutro Reservoir after Midtown Terrace subdivision (1953-60); RPD budgeted $160,000 in 1950s; listed in 1965-67 RPD report

name: Moscone Recreation Center
start_event: Reserved as Lobos Square in 1855 Western Addition plan; later Funston Playground; renamed for Mayor Moscone after 1978
planting_note: 1906 refugee camp; playfield developed 1920s; East Playground 2018

name: Alta Plaza Park
start_event: Reserved as 'Alta Square' by 1855 Van Ness Ordinances (title suit settled 1888)

name: India Basin/Shoreline Park
start_event: Phase 1 (paths, picnic areas, restored wetland) completed 1996
planting_note: Phase 2 trailside landscaping to 2005; 900 Innes expansion opened Oct 2024

name: Lafayette Park
start_event: Reserved in 1855 Van Ness Ordinance (confirmed 1858); Holladay lots inside bought 1935
planting_note: About half improved by 1910; fully built out by WPA 1936-38

name: Ocean View Playground
start_event: 2026-11: original land bought by Supervisors for Playground Commission 1922; more land bought 1926-29 (Playground Commission history, 1928-29 report). Earlier note: Land bought by Supervisors for Playground Commission sometime 1907-1924 (1954 Planning report); playground construction photo dated 1930

name: Potrero Hill Recreation Center
start_event: 2026-11: 9.55-ac Potrero Hill site (22nd-23rd, Arkansas-Missouri) being bought by Playground Commission from 1926 (Playground Commission reports). Earlier note: Existing 'Potrero Hill Playground' improved by WPA late 1930s; photographed 1940; in 1954 inventory

name: Parkside Square
start_event: Reserved as public square in Outside Lands Order No. 800 (1868 map)

name: Holly Park
start_event: Deeded to city 1862 per Bernalwood/Wikipedia (story of purchase by J.G. Fair is doubtful)
planting_note: Holly Park Circle road 1894; proper landscaping incl. eucalyptus 1926

name: Douglass Playground
start_event: 2026-11: land bought by Supervisors and transferred to Playground Commission 1923 (Playground Commission history, 1928-29 report). Earlier note: Land bought by Supervisors for Playground Commission sometime 1907-1924 (1954 Planning report); in use by 1928, graded 1930

name: McCoppin Square
start_event: Reserved in Outside Lands Order No. 800 (1868 map); named for Mayor Frank McCoppin
planting_note: Landscaped with tennis courts and playground 1910s-20s

name: Golden Gate Heights Park
start_event: Land donated by Carl G. Larsen (appeared before Supervisors 30 Oct 1928, died a week later)
planting_note: Listed as 'Sunset Heights Park' in 1954; hilltop forested 1900-1940

name: George Christopher Playground
start_event: Opened 1971 as part of Diamond Heights redevelopment

name: Herz Playground
start_event: Completed 1965 (newly dedicated in FY1965-66)

name: Carl Larsen Park
start_event: Two blocks donated by Carl G. Larsen in early 1920s; Mayor Rolph honored the donation 4 Oct 1926

name: Angelo J. Rossi Playground
start_event: 2026-11: grounds developed by WPA in 1930s; caretaker assigned to Rossi Playground 13 Jul 1939 (1973 commission minutes); proxy 1939. Earlier note: Grounds developed by WPA in 1930s (1954 Planning report); playground photos c.1930 before pool built
planting_note: WPA landscaping 1930s; lawns and trees noted in 1954

name: Youngblood-Coleman Playground
start_event: Housing site abandoned after 1974 accident; 'Galvez Playground Phase I (Youngblood-Coleman)' completed FY1977-78

name: Jefferson Square
start_event: Reserved in 1855 Van Ness Ordinance (Western Addition)

name: Silver Terrace Playground
start_event: 2026-11: land acquired by the city in 1950 for the playground (commission minutes 1957, Res. 2926). Earlier note: Listed as 'Silver Terrace Playfield' in 1954 Planning inventory

name: Raymond Kimball Playground
start_event: Block cleared 1959-60 in Western Addition redevelopment for 'future Raymond Kimbell Playground' (official spelling Kimbell)

name: Gilman Playground
start_event: WPA crews excavated and graded 'Gilman Beach Playground' Dec 1933-Jan 1934

name: Franklin Square
start_event: Established 1868 per SF Parks Alliance (1954 Planning report says Potrero squares laid out with the 1850s Western Addition)

name: Margaret S.Hayward Playground
start_event: South half of Jefferson Square reserved 1855; given to Playground Commission 1907-24 and made a playground

name: Palega Playground
start_event: 2026-11: 'Portola' playground land bought by Supervisors 1924; University Mound/Portola playground partly developed by 1926 (Playground Commission reports). Earlier note: Formerly Portola Playfield (renamed 1996); land bought by Supervisors for Playground Commission sometime 1907-1924 (1954 Planning report); photo 1935

name: Telegraph Hill/Pioneer Park
start_event: Hilltop donated and named Pioneer Park for the 1876 Centennial; later purchases enlarged it

name: Hawk Hill
start_event: 2026-11: Natural Areas program; eminent-domain legislation submitted 1994, 'major portion' (Block 2336 lot 27) reported acquired in the 1996 Open Space report; estimated 1995. Earlier note: 4.5-ac dune-remnant natural area at 14th Ave and Rivera; not in 1954 Planning inventory

name: Aptos Playground
start_event: Playground Commission bought land over 3 years from FY1927-28 (1931 county history timeline)

name: Walter Haas Playground
start_event: 2026-11: 'proposed Walter A. Haas Playground' 1966; construction funded 1973; development Contract RP 647 awarded 1975, phase II (RP 724) 1977-78; estimated 1976. Earlier note: Built in Diamond Heights redevelopment (1961-81); site graded c.1957-60

name: Joseph L. Alioto Performing Arts Piazza
start_event: Civic Center Plaza laid out with Civic Center (1912 bond; City Hall opened Dec 1915; Wikipedia infobox says 1911); renamed for Alioto 28 Oct 1998
planting_note: London plane allees; completed c.1925; rebuilt 1956-60 over Brooks Hall and garage

name: Jackson Playground
start_event: Opened to public 1912 on a reserved Potrero square

name: Potrero del Sol
start_event: Site cleared 1976; park under construction 1980 and called 'new' in 1981 (La Raza Park)

name: Duboce Park
start_event: Van Ness Ordinance hospital-lot reservation dedicated as Duboce Park Sep 1900

name: Ferry Park
start_event: Completed 1975 (Golden Gateway redevelopment); renamed Sue Bierman Park 2007

name: Justin Herman/Embarcadero Plaza
start_event: Completed and opened 1972 (Golden Gateway redevelopment); renamed Embarcadero Plaza 2017

name: Grand View Park
start_event: About an acre at the summit dedicated as parkland 1923; slope lots bought back mid-1970s

name: O'Shaughnessy Hollow
start_event: Acquired by eminent domain in the 1990s (exact year not found; decade midpoint)

name: South Sunset Playground
start_event: 2026-11: possession by court stipulation 1950; dedicated 27 Jun 1951 under the 1947 bond program. Earlier note: Listed in 1954 Planning inventory (40th Ave and Vicente)

name: Brooks Park
start_event: Brooks property (373 Ramsell St) bought FY1966-67 with HUD open-space grant as a natural park
planting_note: Existing trees pruned and labeled before opening

name: Billy Goat Hill
start_event: Officially became a city park 1975 (3.5 ac)

name: Union Square
start_event: Set aside as a public plaza 1850 (Mayor John Geary)

name: Washington Square
start_event: Designated a city square in Jasper O'Farrell's 1847 survey
planting_note: Columbus Ave cut through 1873-75; 1950s redesign with poplars

name: Portsmouth Square
start_event: Used as a public gathering place from 1833; set aside as official plaza 1835 (Plaza de Yerba Buena)

name: South Park
start_event: City took over the private oval park 1897 (laid out 1852-55 by George Gordon as private square)

name: Collins P. Huntington Park
start_event: Huntington mansion site donated by Arabella Huntington 1915

name: Sue Bierman Park
start_event: Same as RPD polygon 'Ferry Park': completed 1975, renamed Sue Bierman Park 2007

name: Monster Park
start_event: Candlestick Park stadium site, not a park: ground broken 1958, opened Apr 1960, named Monster Park 2004-08, last event Aug 2014, demolished by Sep 2015. start_year intentionally blank

name: Salesforce Park
start_event: Rooftop park opened 12 Aug 2018 (closed Sep 2018 - Jul 2019 for beam repairs)

name: Presidio forest
start_event: Army mass tree planting began on Arbor Day 1886 under Maj. W.A. Jones's March 1883 plan (Presidio became a park 1994)
planting_note: 329,975 trees planted by 1892; ~420 ac by 1901 (Monterey pine, cypress, eucalyptus)

name: Crissy Field
start_event: Restored marsh and shoreline park reopened 2001 (NPS and GG National Parks Conservancy)

name: Crissy Field airfield
start_event: Army accepted airfield 24 Jun 1921; closed to airplanes 1974

name: Yerba Buena Gardens
start_event: North block (Mission-Howard) opened 11 Oct 1993; south block opened 1998

name: Lands End
start_event: Became part of Golden Gate National Recreation Area (created 1972); land acquisitions continued into the 1970s
planting_note: Headlands treeless except willows until 1930s, then pine, eucalyptus and cypress planted

name: Sutro Heights
start_event: Sutro family gave estate to city 1938 as a free public park (Sutro opened gardens to public by 1883); city transferred to NPS 1976
planting_note: Gardens planted by Adolph Sutro from 1881-83

name: 10th Ave & Clement Mini Park
start_event: Mini park ('Tenth Avenue' site) built under Contract RP 579 'Various Mini-Parks No. 1' (with Joost, Cayuga and Mullen/Peralta sites); work completed 16 Aug 1971 (Rec & Park Commission minutes 1971)

name: 15th Avenue Steps
start_event: Natural-area lots off the 15th Ave step street (Blocks 1860A/1861A) designated proposed open space 1996 and listed as acquired in the FY1998-99 Open Space report; acquired c.1996-98, estimated 1997

name: 24th & York Mini Park
start_event: Lot 15, Block 4209 (24th St 50 ft west of York) acquisition approved Jan 1971 (Res. 8599); mini park completion reported in the FY1972-73 and FY1973-74 annual reports; estimated 1973

name: 29th & Diamond Open Space
start_event: Diamond Heights redevelopment lot ('1701 Diamond/29th', Block 7536) transferred from the Redevelopment Agency in 1976 with the other Diamond Heights lots (Open Space Program Appendix A: Block 7523/7533/7536, acquired 1976, $400)

name: Adam Rodgers Park
start_event: Built as 'Palou-Jennings Park' in the Hunters Point redevelopment area (development reported FY1973-74; contract changes 1973); named for community leader Adam Rogers by 1977; estimated 1973

name: Alice Chalmers Playground
start_event: Formerly Longfellow Playground (Brunswick & Whittier), rebuilt with 1947 Recreation Bond; renamed 1950; dedicated 31 Mar 1951

name: Alice Marble Tennis Courts
start_event: Courts built on top of the Water Department's Lombard (Greenwich & Hyde) reservoir; opened and dedicated by Alice Marble 18 Nov 1967

name: Alioto Mini Park
start_event: 20th & Capp mini park requested 1968 at start of the city mini-park program; listed as 'Alioto Mini-Park' in the 1971 Plan for Action maintenance schedule; named for Mayor Alioto (1968-76); estimated 1969

name: Allyne Park
start_event: Allyne property (Green & Gough) acquired and opened as a neighborhood park in FY1965-66 (old house demolished, Victorian garden kept); estimated 1966
planting_note: Victorian garden pruned and replanted with period flowers

name: Argonne Playground
start_event: Board of Education permission 1925; Argonne Playground opened May 1926 (Playground Commission reports; RPD: 'established 1926')

name: Arkansas Friendship Garden
start_event: Not found. First appears Feb 1982 when the Parks & Planning Committee heard a report on the garden's program and improvement plan (community garden on the vacated 22nd St strip by Potrero Hill Rec Center); estimated 1982

name: Arlington Community Garden
start_event: 'Arlington Triangle (Glen Park), transfer of surplus DPW property' listed in the 1980 Open Space program; estimated 1980 (garden date not found)

name: Balboa Natural Area
start_event: 'Parcel 4' at Ocean Beach (Block 1592 Lot 3): FY1991-92 Open Space allocation, used as sewer staging; reported co-owned by Rec & Park and DPW in the April 1994 GM report; estimated 1994
planting_note: Native dune landscape plan approved later (2000 report)

name: Bay View Playground
start_event: Land at 3rd, Keith, Carroll and Armstrong bought and transferred to the Playground Commission 1925 (successor to the volunteer-built 1920 playground at 3rd & Jerrold); cleared, field house and trees FY1928-29; renamed Bayview K.C. Jones Playground 2003

name: Beideman & O'Farrell Mini Park
start_event: One of five permanent mini-parks built by the Redevelopment Agency in Western Addition A-2 ('Miniparks (WA-2 - 5 sites) - 1975', reported complete Dec 1975); rebuilt by RPD 1988-89; estimated 1975

name: Berkeley Way Open Space
start_event: Berkeley Way lot (Block 7524) acquired 1977 with Billy Goat Hill from the Redevelopment Agency (Open Space Program Appendix A)

name: Bernal Heights Recreation Center
start_event: Not found. First appears as 'Bernal Playground & Center' (Moultrie & Jarboe, gym on Board of Education land) in the Jan-Jun 1950 commission index; jurisdiction transferred from Board of Education 1956-57 and new fieldhouse then; estimated 1950

name: Broadway Tunnel East Mini Park
start_event: 'Chinatown Mini Park, Broadway Tunnel East Portal' built under Contract RP 626 (awarded 1975); completed 19 Mar 1976

name: Broadway Tunnel West Mini Park
start_event: Mini park on Broadway between Leavenworth and Hyde over the tunnel (Contract RP 604 awarded Jun 1972); completion reported FY1973-74; estimated 1973

name: Brotherhood & Chester Mini Park
start_event: 'Chester Street Mini-Park' on DPW land: 1980 Open Space item to buy a play structure and secure a DPW use agreement; contract RP-941 for the Chester Ave and Head St mini-parks (Brotherhood Way) awarded 1982; estimated 1982

name: Bush & Broderick Mini Park
start_event: Lots 29-30, Block 1053 (Bush between Lyon and Broderick) acquired 1970; mini park dedicated 19 Oct 1971

name: Buchanan Street Mall
start_event: Redevelopment Agency (Western Addition A-2) pedestrian mall by Rai Okamoto with Ruth Asawa fountains; GM report Dec 1975 calls it completed ('1974', $470,000), Japantown context statement says 1976; estimated 1975

name: Cabrillo Playground
start_event: Not found exactly. Board of Education land; not in the 1930 playground list; WPA built field house and courts (date unknown, Living New Deal); 1954 report says Richmond playgrounds were developed in the 1930s; estimated 1937 (WPA era 1935-41)

name: Camp Mather
start_event: Playground Commission's Mountain Camp established 5 Jul 1924 in former Hetch Hetchy construction camp (Tuolumne County); Yosemite Park & Curry camp added 1925

name: Cayuga & Lamartine Mini Park
start_event: Mission Terrace mini park (Cayuga Ave) built under Contract RP 579, completed Aug 1971; 'Cayuga and Lyell' mini park dedicated 19 Oct 1971

name: Cayuga Playground
start_event: Built with 1947 Recreation Bond (under construction 1949-50); dedicated 1 Apr 1951

name: Chesnut & Kearny Open Space
start_event: Not found. First appears in the April 1995 RPD facilities list ('Chestnut & Kearny-Mini, NW Chestnut/Kearny'); former quarry cliff below Telegraph Hill; estimated 1995 (proxy: first listing)

name: Chinese Recreation Center
start_event: New Chinese Recreation Center (Washington & Mason) dedicated 4 Nov 1951; now Betty Ann Ong Recreation Center

name: Clipper Terrace Community Garden
start_event: Not found. Called one of San Francisco's oldest community gardens (KQED); city community-garden program began 1973-74 and most early gardens date 1973-77 (FoundSF); estimated 1975

name: Coleridge Mini Park
start_event: Coleridge Street lots (Block 5615 lots 9, 77) acquired 1985 by Open Space Program; park completed spring 1988

name: Connecticut Friendship Garden
start_event: Not found. Twin of the Arkansas Friendship Garden on the vacated 22nd St strip (first appears 1982); a member wrote of 35+ years of involvement; estimated 1982

name: Corwin Community Garden
start_event: Commission approved use of the southern part of Seward Mini Park by Corwin St as a community garden 21 Dec 1995; estimated 1996

name: Coso & Precita Mini Park
start_event: Not found. Small triangle listed as 'Coso Park, Coso at Coleridge, 0.25 ac' in the 1954 Planning inventory (and 'Coso' in the 1971 maintenance list, 'Coso Triangle' later); proxy: first listing 1954, probably older

name: Cottage Row Mini Park
start_event: Former house site in the Cottage Row alley developed into a park c.1942 (NRHP district / Wikipedia); Japantown context statement treats it as older than the 1960s-70s redevelopment open spaces; estimated 1942

name: Cow Hollow Playground
start_event: Miley playlot (Baker St between Greenwich and Filbert) rebuilt with 1947 bond, named Cow Hollow Playground and dedicated 24 Mar 1951

name: Crags Court Garden
start_event: Diamond Heights redevelopment lot ('8 Crags', Block 7523) transferred from the Redevelopment Agency 1976 with the other Diamond Heights lots

name: Dearborn Community Garden
start_event: Garden planted on a loaned Pepsi bottling-plant parking lot after the plant closed in the 1970s; land deeded to SLUG 1992, later handed to the city; estimated 1977

name: Diamond & Farnum Open Space
start_event: Tax-delinquent Lot 7, Block 7549 (Moffitt & Farnum) acquired for open space 1978 (Commission resolution)

name: Dogpatch/Miller Memorial Garden
start_event: Tax-delinquent Brewster St lots (Block 5556 lots 4-6, 57, 58; Rutledge-Brewster-Franconia, Bernal Heights) acquired 1978 for open space; community garden ('Miller Memorial Grove'); Brewster-Franconia lot added c.1994

name: Dorothy Erskine Park
start_event: Martha Hill lots (Martha/Baden) acquisition approved 1977 (Res. 10930; RPD: acquired 1977; Open Space summary lists 1978); dedicated as Dorothy Erskine Park early 1979

name: DuPont Tennis Courts
start_event: Not found. Listed as 'Clement Tennis Courts' (30th Ave near Clement, school district land) in the 1954 Planning inventory; renamed for Margaret Osborne duPont 1959; proxy: first listing 1954

name: Duncan & Castro Open Space
start_event: Duncan and Castro lots (Block 6590) acquired 1979 (Open Space Program Appendix A; acquisition ratified 1977-78)

name: Edgehill Mountain

name: Esprit Park

name: Eureka Valley Playground
start_event: Land at 19th & Collingwood (Block 2694) bought 1950 for a 1947-bond playground; listed in 1954 inventory; new center named and dedicated 1956

name: Everson & Digby Lots
start_event: Diamond Heights parcel 'Everson St, W of Digby' added to the city open-space plan Jan 1977 (Diamond Heights lots transferred from the Redevelopment Agency 1976-77); estimated 1977

name: Excelsior Playground
start_event: Excelsior Homestead Playground land (Persia, Russia, Madrid, Edinburgh) bought by the Supervisors July 1911

name: Fairmont Plaza
start_event: Not found. RPD-owned undeveloped 'Fairmount Park' (Fairmount & San Miguel) already in 1947 commission minutes; owned but undeveloped in 1954; proxy: first mention 1947

name: Father Alfred E. Boeddeker Park
start_event: Central City Park site bought 1978-85 by Open Space Program; dedicated 1 May 1985

name: Fay Park
start_event: Fay house and Thomas Church garden (1957) bequeathed by Mary Fay Berrigan; accepted by city 1998; opened to the public 2006

name: Fillmore & Turk Mini Park
start_event: One of five permanent mini-parks built by the Redevelopment Agency in Western Addition A-2 (reported complete Dec 1975); estimated 1975

name: Fulton Playground
start_event: Not found exactly. Board of Education land; graded as a new playground and developed by the WPA in the 1930s (1954 Planning report; Living New Deal); not in the 1930 playground list; estimated 1937

name: Garden for the Environment
start_event: Demonstration garden at 7th Ave & Lawton teaching since 1990

name: Garfield Square
start_event: Designated 1868 (Order No. 800) as a city hall/library lot; opened as a park 1884 on the former Recreation Grounds ballpark

name: Geneva Avenue Strip
start_event: Lot 27, Block 6964 (Geneva & Delano) transferred from DPW to Rec & Park for open space 1979

name: Golden Gate & Steiner Mini Park
start_event: One of five permanent mini-parks built by the Redevelopment Agency in Western Addition A-2 (reported complete Dec 1975); estimated 1975

name: Grand View Open Space
start_event: 'Golden Gate Heights' open space at Noriega & 15th Ave (Block 1928B) acquired 1981 ($520,000)

name: Grattan Playground
start_event: Land at Stanyan & Rivoli bought 1950; built with 1947 Recreation Bond and dedicated 27 Mar 1952

name: Hamilton Playground
start_event: Hamilton Square was one of the squares reserved when the Western Addition was laid out in 1855 (1954 Planning report); deeded by Park Commission to Playground Commission June 1911

name: Hilltop Park
start_event: 'Ridgetop (Hilltop) Park' in the Hunters Point redevelopment area dedicated by Mayor Moscone 23 Sep 1978
